items.title: Liverpool v Nottingham Forest: Premier League – live
items.summary: Live updates from Anfield 12.30pm kick-off (BST) Email Scott | Reds finalise £123m Barcola deal The teams are out! Liverpool all in red, Forest wearing a third-choice shirt that looks awfully like a recent Manchester City number. You’ll Never Walk Alone rings out, as Liverpool principal owner John Henry and the new vice-chairman Amit Bhatia watch from the stand. We’ll be off in a minute … and that minute will see fans remember the legendary Kevin Keegan, the star of Bill Shankly’s second great team, who recently passed. The warmest applause from all four corners of the ground, a mosaic on the Kop that reads KEVIN 7, and a chant of One Kevin Keegan. On the subject of Forest and big-money transfers … David Ornstein of the Athletic was on TNT Sports earlier, reporting the possibility of their buying 19-year-old midfield prospect Harrison Armstrong from Everton for £40m. Should that come to pass, it’ll probably result in the Hill Dickinson toppling into the Mersey, but only after the whole structure is launched a couple of miles into the air by the steam from Everton supporters’ lugs. Armstrong is extremely highly rated, but Forest have pockets full of cash after selling Elliot Anderson to Manchester City, so this one is worth keeping an eye on. Continue reading...

items.title: Alonso gets Chelsea’s priorities right by ditching Sánchez for winner Martínez | Jacob Steinberg
items.summary: Signing of World Cup winner adds to sense that this is the summer when BlueCo got serious in transfer market Carlo Cudicini was a very good goalkeeper. However, José Mourinho was ruthless when he became Chelsea manager in 2004. Very good was not good enough. Mourinho wanted the best and one of the main factors behind the Portuguese winning the Premier League during his first season in charge was the decision to replace Cudicini with Petr Cech. There is an old line about a great goalkeeper being worth 15 points a season. It is not for nothing, for instance, that Brian Clough regarded Peter Shilton as one of his most important signings at Nottingham Forest. Shilton was key when Forest defied the odds by winning the Division One title in 1978 and there are plenty of other examples of promising teams taking the next step only after buying a top No 1. Continue reading...

items.title: La RAAL et Saint-Trond concurrencés : un autre club pousse pour Arnaud Bodart
items.summary: Après avoir quitté le Standard en janvier 2025 avec l'envie de franchir un nouveau cap dans sa carrière, Arnaud Bodart pourrait déjà signer son retour en Jupiler Pro League un an et demi plus tard. La RAAL est intéressée par ses services, mais aussi Saint-Trond, qui se met déjà à la recherche d'un nouveau portier suite au départ plus que probable de Leo Kokubo vers Parme. Et voilà qu'un club étranger entre dans la danse.
